summary.headline: Veerhealth Care targets ~Rs 100 crore FY27 turnover and Rs 5-6 crore PAT after Q1 FY27 revenue of ~Rs 25 crore and PAT of Rs 1.25 crore.
summary.overview: Management said Q1 FY27 revenue was about Rs 25 crore, already exceeding the full FY26 turnover of about Rs 30-33 crore, and reported Q1 profit of Rs 125 lakh. Growth was attributed mainly to a contract manufacturing relationship with an Indian FMCG brand (onboarded November 2025), with the US export business up about 20% YoY as stated. Capacity utilisation is 65-75%, with three new lines being added and full utilisation targeted by Q1 FY28. The company also disclosed a preferential issue under way, with proceeds expected in about two months. Management gave no quantified order book beyond general statements of strong exports and contract manufacturing orders.

financial_highlights.change: Management said it crossed full FY26 turnover in a single quarter; no precise YoY figure given
Figures stated inconsistently in the call

segments.name: Contract manufacturing (CDMO, personal care and oral care)
segments.commentary: About 70% of Q1 FY27 revenue; supplies face care and skin care products to a top-three Indian FMCG brand under a contract since November 2025, with three products rolled out and more SKUs planned. A leading Indian pharmacy chain (7,000+ outlets) is another contract customer for hair and oral care.

segments.name: Exports (US, East Africa, Middle East)
segments.commentary: About 20% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Serves a US institutional supplier with government LTAs; management said shipments run at 6-7 a month and could rise to 12-15 after expansion. Exports go to US and East African markets directly or via merchant exporters.

segments.name: Own brand AYUVEER
segments.commentary: About 10% of Q1 FY27 revenue; 42+ formulations across hair, skin, body and oral care, sold on Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra and the company website.

segments.name: Veer Plast (plastic and toothbrush division)
segments.commentary: Newly launched in-house injection and blow moulding for bottles, caps, canisters and enclosures, plus toothbrush moulding and stuffing; supplies toothbrushes to the US customer. No revenue split disclosed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 turnover target of ~Rs 100 crore and PAT of ~Rs 5-6 crore.
Three new manufacturing lines being added; by December 2026 the company expects 5-6 personal care lines and 3 oral care lines (from 4 and 2 currently).
Expansion expected to complete around December 2026, which management said would drive a further spike in contract manufacturing volumes.
Full capacity utilisation targeted in Q1 FY28.
Preferential equity allotment expected to be completed within about two months; management said no further equity fundraise is planned this year.
capex_capacity: Current Vapi capacity utilisation stated at 65-70% in one answer and 70-75% in another; expected to reach about 90% after expansion and 100% by Q1 FY28.
Acquired an additional 30,000 sq ft adjacent land in October 2024, taking production area from about 60,000 to 90,000 sq ft; a further ~60,000 sq ft of capacity was also referred to.
A 5 metric ton manufacturing capacity was said to be coming in about three weeks from the call.
Adding R&D lab, laboratory, warehouse and store capacity alongside the new lines.
Plans to automate and scale the facility to reduce cost per unit.
demand_pricing: Management said the FMCG brand is among the top three brands on local marketplaces and that the relationship is a major growth driver.
Management said the US institutional customer holds long-term supply agreements (LTAs) with the US government and orders remained steady despite tariffs and freight issues.
An Indo-Canadian company supplying airlines and five-star hotels placed a first trial order; first batch of oral care products has been supplied and audit and site visit are complete.
Raw material cost impact from the Gulf conflict was described as limited because the principal customer negotiates and bears raw material prices under contract manufacturing.
Management said USFDA approval shortens onboarding with large Indian FMCG companies.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the revenue spike and how much came from repeat orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed growth mainly to the Indian FMCG contract manufacturing relationship from November 2025 and said US repeat orders continue under government LTAs, with exports up about 20%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q1 revenue mix and can the run rate be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix was 70% contract manufacturing, 20% exports and 10% own brand. Management said Q1 was not a one-time spike and pointed to expansion by December and more brands being onboarded by the FMCG principal.

qa_highlights.question: What is current capacity utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Stated at 65-70% in one answer and 70-75% in another, with about 90% expected after expansion and 100% targeted by Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is any equity fundraise planned and what is the status of the warrant money?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no further equity fundraise is planned this year; a preferential allotment is underway and the money is expected in about two months. It disputed the question's reference to warrants.

qa_highlights.question: Is promoter holding planned to increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said an increase is under consideration and may be reviewed and implemented in coming quarters, without a figure given.

qa_highlights.question: How will receivables, payables and working capital be managed as orders scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the principal customer supports receivables and payables with quick payments and funding facilities and helps procure large-ticket raw materials, so large orders were not seen as a challenge.

risks_watch: FY27 target of ~Rs 100 crore implies roughly four times the Q1 run rate, dependent on capacity coming online by December 2026.
Heavy concentration in a few customers (one Indian FMCG principal, one US institutional supplier, one pharmacy chain) with no quantified order book.
Inconsistent figures: FY26 turnover stated as ~Rs 30 crore and ~Rs 33 crore; the warrant versus preferential issue description was contested in the call.
Working capital and receivables/payables rising significantly in FY26; no cash flow or balance sheet data was provided.
Promoter holding described as very low by an analyst; no timeline or quantum for increase.
Canada and hospitality opportunity is at trial stage only and is not yet in the revenue targets.
Q1 profit margin of about 5% (Rs 1.25 crore on Rs 25 crore) against the implied FY27 PAT margin of about 5-6% should be checked against the full-year target.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth, with management repeatedly asserting that targets are achievable. Answers on capacity utilisation, promoter holding and the warrant or preferential issue were less precise and inconsistent in places, and no detailed order book or cash flow data was offered.
key_quotes: So, over the financial year 26-27, we expect to achieve a turnover of approximately 100 crores.
We have crossed the entire previous financial US turnover within a single quarter of the current financial year.
So, the orders are going good.

adds.what: 3 new manufacturing lines (personal care to 5-6 lines from 4; oral care to 3 from 2)

growth.why: Management targets ~Rs 100 crore FY27 turnover and PAT of Rs 5-6 crore, backed by three new lines due around December 2026 and an FMCG contract already running, but no quantified order book was given and Q1 revenue growth YoY was not stated.
